business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fractional CFO Advisory and Multicurrency Ledger Bookkeeping

Luxembourg-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, as amended by the 2009 Protocol
Luxembourg-China Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion in respect of Taxes on Income and Capital (1980)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the practical functioning of the RBE; CSSF Circular 17/650 on AML/CFT risk-based supervision; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, governing the SCSp.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted access by competent authorities and obliged entities under AML/CFT law; no general public access following CJEU case-law on beneficial ownership registers)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority in the country of issuance, followed by notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille through the competent Apostille authority of the issuing state; for non-Hague states, consular legalization by the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each individual UBO, general partner, and limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company, licensed bank, or national identity authority in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification, then Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable to the issuing state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration and Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate UBO, corporate general partner, or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent authority in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization by the relevant foreign authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified constitutional documents of each corporate partner, including articles of incorporation, memorandum, by-laws, and current certificate of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or statutory corporate filing authority in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified English or French translation to be filed where the original is not in an official EU language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Tax Residence for each corporate partner relying on treaty protection or claiming Luxembourg tax transparency
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National tax authority of the country of tax residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as required by the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming account history and standing of the partner or shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the existing banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed and notarized confirmation, with Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the receiving Luxembourg bank or RCS filing requires it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg formation agent and domiciliation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution, or Luxembourg notary where execution occurs in Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if executed abroad; must be in French, German, English, or accompanied by a certified translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, authorised signatories, and material counterparties against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists for USD or US-counterparty exposure, the Luxembourg operational list of financial sanctions, and commercial PEP databases; PEPs, family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring; simplified due diligence is permissible only for demonstrably low-risk relationships and never waives UBO identification; all screening results, risk ratings, and supporting documents must be retained in the KYC file for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online e-Filing and name availability portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filings and registry extracts are in French, German, or Luxembourgish; English may be used in the partnership agreement but the legal-form suffix must be 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale'; where the requested name is in non-Latin script, a certified transliteration into a Latin-script official EU language must be filed; the name must be available, not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and not misleading as to legal form, regulated activity, public authority, or State endorsement.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
CSSF / PFS / Agent Financier / Financial Regulator
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its Luxembourg counsel must re-verify the LBR name-search result and submit a written reconsideration request to the RCS registrar within 15 calendar days, attaching legal arguments and evidence of distinctiveness; if the registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg sitting in commercial matters within one month of the formal refusal, through an avocat à la Cour; the appeal should request annulment of the refusal and an order for registration; statutory court costs and counsel fees apply, and the parallel filing of an alternative cleared name is recommended to avoid formation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mailbox-only or teleport virtual office without a fixed Luxembourg address and without a local authorised representative is not permissible for a Luxembourg SCSp claiming tax residence or substance. A virtual-office arrangement will be accepted only through a licensed or recognised Luxembourg domiciliation agent providing a physical street address, mail-handling facility, legal service reception point, and a contractual undertaking to retain corporate records; for the outsourced virtual CFO and bookkeeping commercial model, the structure should maintain a local registered office, an authorised Luxembourg representative or agent, and adequate minutes or partnership records evidencing substance and economic activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 5% probability over a 12-month period for a non-regulated low-risk SCSp with no financial-sector licensing requirement; probability rises to approximately 25% over 12 months where the SCSp seeks a certificate of tax residence, claims treaty benefits, conducts progressive financing activities, or is subjected to a risk-based substance audit by the Luxembourg tax authority, RCS registrar, or judicial authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Part VI (Articles 101-1 to 101-14 on the Société en Commandite Spéciale), introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; general partnership provisions in Articles 99 to 124.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operating the e-Justice/LBR portal and the RBE register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive deed (acte constitutif/statuts), executed as a private deed or notarial deed, followed by registration application on the RCS via the LBR e-Justice portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Luxembourg law imposes no statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; the partnership agreement freely fixes the capital (cash or in-kind). Subscribed capital must be effectively made available to the partnership treasury and evidenced by a bank attestation for the RCS file; no escrow or blocked account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial partnership interests in the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) be fully subscribed and accepted by the partners as set forth in the executed partnership agreement; RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Manager (Gérant), with exclusive authority to open and operate bank accounts, engage employees, and execute client contracts for virtual CFO and bookkeeping services; RESOLVED, that the Manager undertake all registrations with the Luxembourg Business Registers, the Ministry of the Economy, VAT administration, and social security authorities; RESOLVED, that said appointments and registered office be effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the SCSp Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (if real estate contributed) or private deed signed by all partners; filing via LBR e-Justice portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French or English, covering SCSp name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate purpose (fractional CFO advisory, multicurrency bookkeeping), capital schedule, general partner (Gérant) powers, and profit-sharing clauses. Execute by notarial deed before a Luxembourg notary if real estate is contributed; otherwise execute as a private deed (sous seing privé) with original wet-ink signatures or advanced e-signatures compliant with Luxembourg law.
required_dossiers: Valid passports of all partners and the Gérant
Proof of residential address (utility bill/bank statement)
Draft partnership agreement
CVs and criminal record extracts (casier judiciaire) of the Gérant
Notarized power of attorney if any signatory acts remotely
AML/KYC questionnaire if requested by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or LBR queries the deed for incompleteness, issue a supplementary rectification act or re-execute the affected signature pages; if name conflicts arise, submit 2-3 alternative reserved names for priority re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Luxembourg Bank Account and Effectuate Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., BNP Paribas Luxembourg, Intesa Sanpaolo Private Banking, Société Générale Bank & Trust)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership deed, beneficial ownership information and KYC documentation to the selected bank. Open a EUR-denominated corporate account in the SCSp name, deposit the subscribed capital, and obtain a written attestation of account opening and deposit confirmation (attestation de souscription/dépôt) required for RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
Passports and proof of address of signatories and beneficial owners
Bank account application form
Business plan and projected income statement for the virtual CFO services
Declaration of economic purpose if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays account opening, escalate to the bank's compliance committee with a further AML file; alternatively use a licensed Luxembourg e-money institution for the initial deposit attestation. Engage a local domiciliation agent to support KYC documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration Application with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online registration via the LBR e-Justice portal: provide the SCSp identification, attach the signed partnership deed, the notary attestation (where applicable), list of Gérants with their acceptance, registered office consent, and the bank deposit attestation. Pay the statutory filing fee upon submission.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership deed (scan of original)
Bank attestation of capital contribution
Declaration of the registered office address (domiciliation acceptance letter)
Identity documents of the Gérant and general partner
Power of attorney if filed by a local agent
Bank deposit attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (bordereau de rejet), respond within 10 business days with corrected documents or clarifications on the corporate purpose; if registration is refused, correct the indicated objections and resubmit; fees may be waived for a single corrected re-filing within the same request cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the authorities automatically publish the notice of incorporation in RESA via the LBR electronic compendium. Verify that the published excerpt contains the exact SCSp name, registered office, purpose, and identifying data of the Gérant, as this publication constitutes the legal opposability event.
required_dossiers: No separate submission; direct electronic transmission from the RCS registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA excerpt contains typographical or data errors, file a written correction request with the RCS registry clerk, attaching the registration certificate and correct data; corrections are processed within 3-5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for the Business Operating Permit (Autorisation d'Etablissement) and Tax/Social Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes; submission via MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment permit application for the commercial activity (virtual CFO and bookkeeping services). Register simultaneously with the VAT administration (Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA) and with the social security authority (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale – CCSS) for employer affiliation.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration
Police record extract of the Gérant (casier judiciaire)
Evidence of professional qualifications or equivalent experience
Partnership deed and extract of the Gérant appointment
Completed business license application form
VAT registration form (Formulaire 1 and annexes)
CCSS employer affiliation declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is queried or deferred, furnish supplementary evidence of professional competence or diplomas within the statutory response period; if denied, lodge a written appeal to the Minister of the Economy within two months and concurrently rectify the application file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 days of RCS registration, declare all beneficial owners (physical persons owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp capital or voting rights). File the declaration electronically via the LBR RBE portal, attaching the supporting identification data and the capacity in which each beneficial owner acts.
required_dossiers: RBE online declaration form
Partnership agreement extract identifying ownership percentages
Passport copies of each beneficial owner
Supporting corporate chart or transfer records if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE filing is rejected, correct and resubmit the declaration within 15 days; if late-filing penalties are threatened, submit a reasoned request for mitigation with proof of attempted timely filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes (via MyGuichet.lu)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Operation Permit) for commercial services under the Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Exempt (Category C, office-based activity): no full EIA Report required for a pure virtual CFO and bookkeeping office with no industrial installations; a simple operational declaration may be required if local zoning permits are triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only operations with no significant point-source discharges; any wastewater discharge to municipal sewers must comply with local municipal discharge bylaws and the general wastewater standards of the Law of 21 March 2017; electronic waste, paper, batteries and packaging must be segregated per waste management provisions; VOC emissions from office equipment remain below applicable thresholds (Grand-Ducal Regulation on VOC limits); energy audit obligations apply if the enterprise exceeds the EU Energy Efficiency Directive threshold (annual consumption >100 TJ).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the Grand-Ducal Regulation on workplace fire safety (mandatory evacuation plan, fire extinguishers, and building operator certificate); structural safety inspection evidenced by the leaseholder's building occupancy certificate; occupational health and workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering lighting, ergonomics, and electrical safety; mandatory employer registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for workplace accident coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for statutory registration; official digital gateway: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu) and the AEDT electronic filing portal (eCDF).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Instruct a Luxembourg resident certified public accountant (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) to draft and file the SCSp constitutive act; Step 2: Register the SCSp in the RCS in Luxembourg and obtain the national identification number (matricule), which constitutes the statutory TIN for the partnership; Step 3: File VAT registration Form 46/V with the AEDT via the eCDF/MyGuichet portal to obtain a VAT number in the format LU-8 digits (no per-partner VAT auto-registration is required as the SCSp is fiscally transparent); Step 4: Ensure each partner notifies the ACD of its foreign TIN/residence so that profits are apportioned and reported by the partners individually, not by the SCSp; Step 5: Maintain a Luxembourg registered office, a local authorized representative (personne de contact), accounting ledgers in EUR, and the partnership's bank/payment-rail settlement records (Stripe_Billing and Wise) for substance documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent under the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 (as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013) and Article 175 LIR — profits, losses, and income are allocated directly to the partners in accordance with the partnership agreement; the SCSp itself is not an income-tax taxpayer, and assets/liabilities are attributed to the partners for Luxembourg tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no US-style 'check-the-box' election under Luxembourg law; the SCSp's transparency is mandatory. Available statutory options include: (i) an application under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law to form a VAT group (assujetti unique) with affiliated Luxembourg entities; (ii) designation of a managing general partner as the sole accountable person for wage-tax and withholding declarations; (iii) partner-level elections under Article 161 LIR aligning the partners' fiscal year with the SCSp's financial year; and (iv) disclosure/election mechanisms under Article 168quater LIR (ATAD hybrid mismatch rules) to neutralise any conflicting foreign classifications of the SCSp. Non-resident partners may further file a US check-the-box election (Form 8832) if they are US taxpayers, but such election has no effect on the Luxembourg transparency treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Luxembourg Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA), governed by the Luxembourg Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, implementing the EU VAT Directive (2006/112/EC).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 statutory threshold for non-established suppliers: any foreign entity or partnership making taxable supplies in Luxembourg (B2B services subject to Luxembourg VAT or B2C supplies physically performed in Luxembourg) must register immediately. Luxembourg-established businesses may benefit from the small-business franchise exemption where their annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000, provided the supplies are domestic B2C services/goods; the franchise does not apply to intra-EU acquisitions, distance sales, or services supplied to VAT-identified EU customers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: As of the current filing year, no real-time B2B fiscal clearance, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping mandate applies in Luxembourg for services such as virtual CFO advising. B2G invoices addressed to Luxembourg public-sector entities must be submitted electronically in the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format. All VAT returns and recapitulative statements are filed electronically via the AEDT's eCDF/MyGuichet interface (monthly, quarterly, or per transaction depending on turnover), and the ACD may require SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) electronic accounting data on request or for large taxpayers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% with full input VAT deduction applies to: (i) physical export of goods outside the EU if the goods leave the EU within prescribed time limits and the supplier holds a customs export declaration; (ii) intra-EU B2B supplies of the virtual CFO services, for which Luxembourg VAT is not chargeable and the customer's Member State applies the reverse charge, provided the customer communicates a valid EU VAT identification number; and (iii) services supplied to customers established outside the EU (territorial outside of scope, not technically zero-rated) where the place of supply is the customer's country. For the SCSp, the standard service export will be outside scope for non-EU customers and reverse-charged for EU B2B customers; documentary status-evidence is mandatory to validate the customer's identification, including the financial institution's (Stripe/Wise) settlement records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Luxembourg customs export declaration (SAD) and transport evidence (Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR) — applicable only if physical goods are incidentally exported by the SCSp; not required for pure virtual CFO services
Signed engagement letter / service contract stating the customer's country of establishment and the cross-border (offshore) nature of the service
Customer's valid EU VAT identification number (verified via VIES) or, for non-EU customers, an official foreign tax identification number / Chamber of Commerce extract
Stripe_Billing and Wise transaction reports, together with BIC/SWIFT inward remittance certificates evidencing payment from the non-Luxembourg customer
EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) filed electronically within the applicable calendar month where intra-EU B2B services are supplied
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating or outside-scope treatment is improperly claimed, the AEDT assesses Luxembourg VAT at 17% on the gross consideration together with moratorium interest at 0.6% per month of delay; deliberate non-disclosure attracts an administrative penalty of 10-20% of the tax evaded and an additional fine of EUR 250-10,000 against the responsible general partner. Fraudulent documentary claims (false customs declarations or fictitious invoices) expose the SCSp and its general partner to criminal fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years, with the normal five-year assessment period extended to ten years. Retroactive clawbacks of repaid input VAT and denial of deduction rights apply where the export evidence is defective, and uncollected foreign receivables remaining beyond the 180-day benchmark without commercial justification may be recharacterised as Luxembourg-source income under CFC/PE substance rules.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), with financial-sector supervision exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and anti-money-laundering intelligence by the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF); monetary policy is delegated to the European Central Bank within the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; Luxembourg operates no exchange-control or capital-authorisation regime for either current-account or capital-account flows. The euro (EUR) is the sole legal tender; service fees, partner capital contributions, and profit allocations may be freely converted into any internationally traded currency. Profit-remittance hurdles are absent at entity level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and distributions carry no Luxembourg withholding tax; the only practical gate is the banking counterparty's documentary due diligence covering source of funds and partner identification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender obligation for export or service receipts. Invoices issued by the SCSp may be collected in any freely convertible currency and retained or converted at the operator's discretion; only CRF AML reporting thresholds apply to physical-cash movements and unusual transactions under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for operational cash-flow accounts only, with strict legal constraints. The SCSp may onboard with EEA-authorised electronic money institutions - Wise Europe / Wise Payments Europe S.A. (authorised in Belgium and Ireland, passporting into Luxembourg) and Stripe Payments Europe Ltd (authorised by the Central Bank of Ireland) - under Directive 2009/110/EC. Such accounts are e-money wallets, not credit-institution deposits; they are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme and may not hold third-party escrow, partner capital escrow, or legal-charge cash. Consequently, Stripe Billing payouts and Wise disbursements are restricted to operational turnover; all partner capital, reserved liquidity, and client-fee escrow funds must be held with a CSSF-regulated Tier-1 credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible but operationally conditioned. CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the AML Law allow non-face-to-face identification where the bank applies augmented controls (qualified electronic signature, video interview, geolocation, and certified RCS extracts). In practice, BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, and Société Générale Luxembourg require at least one physical or video-verified appearance of the general partner (GP) and of any individual UBO holding 10% or more; corporate GPs must additionally submit constitutional documents, a UBO declaration, and board resolutions appointing signatories. Because the SCSp lacks legal personality, the account is opened in the SCSp's name with full representative powers evidenced by the limited partnership agreement and a bank-provided signature mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO located in an FATF grey-listed or high-risk third country, or indirect sanction pegging through an intermediate holding layer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO chain chart with percentage breakdown per partner; sanction-screening clearances (World-Check or Dow Jones) dated within 30 days; source-of-wealth evidence comprising bank statements, tax returns, and audited financials; partnership deed with lawful-payee clauses; notarised confirmation of Luxembourg domiciliation and economic substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque nominee or silent-partner arrangement concealing the true economic owner of the SCSp interest.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Nominee and fiduciary declarations disclosing the underlying economic owner; written renunciation of economic benefits signed by the nominee; CSSF-compliant organisational chart approved by the GP; Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the enforceability of the SCSp designation-of-manager and transfer-restriction clauses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status, adverse media, or criminal/fiscal record of any partner or director at the time of onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed PEP declaration supported by an independent media-profile due-diligence report; legitimate-source documentation (employment contract, buy-out agreement, inheritance deed); criminal-record and tax good-standing certificates from the country of residence; written commitment to enhanced periodic reviews with senior-management approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dormant-shell profile with low or non-verifiable economic substance for the stated virtual-CFO activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement or regulated domiciliation arrangement with an operating substance plan; staffing evidence for the virtual-CFO business (subcontractor agreements, payroll, workspaces); client engagement letters and invoicing projections under ISIC 6920; Luxembourg VAT registration certificate and EORI or statistical filings demonstrating active operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound funds originating from crypto exchanges, unregulated money-service businesses, or third-party wires that do not match declared client invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client contracts and invoice ledger establishing payment-to-invoice mapping; crypto exchange and wallet reports with chain-analysis clearance; written undertaking by the GP excluding third-party settlement; copies of all CRF threshold reports filed in respect of the flagged transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner contributions are remitted by SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR, with Field 70 stating 'Apport en capital - SCSp contribution per LPA [date]' and referencing the RCS registration number, plus ISO 20022 purpose code CAPC (capital payment) or INTC (intra-company) where applicable. The receiving bank requires the signed limited partnership agreement, the extrait du RCS, partner resolutions authorising the injection, and a UBO certificate. No BCL, CSSF, or CRF prior approval is required; EUR contributions are not monitored, and non-EUR funds are converted to EUR at spot with ECB reference-rate pricing. Source-of-funds evidence (partner bank statements and tax confirmations) must accompany all first-time contributions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: SWIFT MT103 (Fields 50K remitter, 70 invoice and contract references) for cross-border USD, GBP, and CHF settlements; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant with purpose codes SUPP, BUSB, SALA, and DIVI for EEA vendor payments, payroll, and partner distributions. Commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) and standby LCs are available through Tier-1 relationship banks as contingent instruments for large client-fee contracts, though non-standard for ISIC 6920 advisory disbursements. Wise and Stripe operate as secondary channels for low-value, high-frequency multicurrency payouts with virtual-IBAN reconciliation into the EUR master account. All outbound EUR wires settle within TARGET2; non-EUR wires require value-date discipline and daily FX limit monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla physically settled EUR/USD and EUR/GBP FX forwards with CSSF-regulated counterparties under ISDA 2002/CSA documentation; no Luxembourg authorisation requirement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted-currency exposures (CNY, INR, BRL) booked via the Luxembourg bank's London or New York branch for balance-sheet protection of non-EUR client-fee receivables; subject to EMIR trade-reporting and clearing-threshold assessment.

Cross-currency swaps (CCIRS) converting future committed capital draws or partner loan notes into EUR; LEI required; EMIR clearing and trade-reporting obligations apply unless the ancillary-activity hedging exemption is satisfied.
Roll-over currency swaps with a CSSF credit institution as a working-capital line matched to forecast multicurrency receivables.

Vanilla FX options (EUR call/USD put and reverse) for insurance-style downside protection on non-EUR client invoices, with premiums settled via the bank treasury desk and no speculative-trading mandate for the SCSp.

Wise and Stripe auto-conversion at mid-market rate for operational pockets capped at 10% of monthly turnover, with daily reconciliation to the EUR master account to prevent disguised speculative FX positions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing duty; any change must be filed within one month; annual confirmation requested by the register within 15 days after the end of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; criminal penalties of up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment for managing partners in case of intentional non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual filing of financial statements (annual accounts) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts and no later than seven months after the end of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court summons and fine up to EUR 1,500; continued non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur les sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD / Luxembourg tax authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of the year following the taxable year if filed electronically; extension to 30 June upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 250; late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; additional penalties up to 10% of tax due if filed after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal, ICC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as corporate income tax return filing deadline (typically by 31 March with extension to 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same penalty regime as corporate income tax; late-payment interest 0.8% per month; collective assessment of ICC with final tax bill

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (impôt sur la fortune, IF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Minimum net wealth tax applies (EUR 3,000 for SCSp engaged in financial or holding activities); late-payment interest 0.8% per month; penalties similar to income tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (déclaration annuelle de TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 250; late-payment interest 1.5% per month; potential 10% increase of VAT due

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the registered office (déclaration annuelle / re-registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Optional annual confirmation within 30 days following the anniversary of registration; required update on change of registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update registered office may result in administrative penalties and potential strike-off after formal warnings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of the annual list of partners (liste des associés) for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed initially upon incorporation; any change in partners or capital must be filed within one month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000; inability to assert partnership rights against third parties; possible judicial strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if the SCSp exceeds two of the three following thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 6.0 million, net turnover above EUR 12.0 million, average number of employees above 50; also mandatory if the SCSp is part of a consolidated group above group thresholds; audit may also be required by the partnership agreement, investor request, or CRA regulatory status
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts; IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for consolidated accounts only; certain financial SCSp structures may apply special accounting rules

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain a register of beneficial owners at its registered office; file the UBO declaration with the RBE within one month of any transfer or change; RBE confirmation is carried out annually by the LBR; the managing partners must confirm the exactness of the UBO register upon each annual filing; for the SCSp, all direct and indirect partners holding 25% or more are considered beneficial owners
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors/Managing Partners (Registre des gérants)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per year for a certified audit of a typical SCSp

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: SCSp is fiscally transparent and not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax at entity level; resident corporate partners are taxed at combined headline rate of 24.94% (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% of CIT + municipal business tax up to 6.75% for Luxembourg City).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level tax holidays; partners may benefit from Luxembourg participation exemption on qualifying dividend and capital gain income, and from treaty relief; transparent income retains source nature.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No CIT return or e-filing portal is required for the SCSp itself because it lacks Luxembourg corporate income tax subjectivity; any required declarations are filed by partners via MyGuichet.lu or the Luxembourg direct tax administration portal (eSpace).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Partner-level returns follow the partner's own taxable year; where a Luxembourg tax return is filed, the statutory deadline is generally 30 June following the year of the fiscal year-end, with automatic extension to 31 December if filed electronically, subject to extension requests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identity and Luxembourg/foreign tax status of each partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report only Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real property, if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the SCSp's taxable income or loss to each partner under the partnership agreement and transparent accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report the agreed NA – not necessarily pro rata – allocation, subject to anti-abuse and substance verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of Luxembourg dividend, interest, or royalty withholding, where the SCSp is resident payer for withholding purposes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim treaty relief or refund through the Luxembourg withholding tax refund procedure, attaching a valid Tax Residency Certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file a required partner-level return attracts a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of tax due; daily delinquency penalties may apply at EUR 1,000 per annum and up to EUR 5,000 for repeated non-filing; statutory interest on late tax payment accrues at 0.6% per month.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% at SCSp level for distributions to partners because the vehicle is fiscally transparent; if treated as a Luxembourg resident company due to disguised equity characterization, the statutory rate would be 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the payee must file an exemption or refund application with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes) using Form B or Form 22, accompanied by the official Tax Residency Certificate from the jurisdiction of residence; Luxembourg tax authorities may require beneficial ownership documentation and an active economic substance declaration for the SCSp.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Luxembourg entity generally incur 25% withholding tax absent treaty (EU Interest-Royalty Directive may provide 0% where conditions are met); interest payments are usually not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax unless profit-participating or related-party hybrid financing is used; treaty rates for EU affiliates typically lower to 0–5% for royalties and 0% for qualifying interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File in Luxembourg is due when transactions with related parties exceed EUR 1,000,000 per year (goods) or EUR 500,000 (services); Master File is required when a worldwide group has consolidated turnover exceeding EUR 50,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The SCSp must maintain genuine economic substance in Luxembourg where it performs 'virtual CFO' services, including real management, employees, business premises, and records; although SCSp is not directly within Luxembourg's ESR box of the AIFM/UCITS regime, the tax administration applies the substance-over-form doctrine and OECD BEPS standards to deny treaty benefits to shell or letterbox entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring an SCSp to artificially route fees and retain profits without economic substance, or falsely claiming treaty benefits despite no active activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of income plus late interest at 0.6% monthly; administrative penalty up to 10% of evaded tax; criminal penalty up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for wilful fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or managing partners may be compulsorily wound up, held jointly and severally liable for taxes when assets are stripped, subject to travel bans and, upon criminal conviction, imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Running treasury and virtual CFO functions from another jurisdiction with no real presence, employees, or decisions in Luxembourg while claiming Luxembourg treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Luxembourg residence certificate; disqualification from EU directives and tax treaty relief; retroactive penalty tax of 50% on disallowed deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for restitution of all diverted taxes, including personal seizure of bank accounts; professional ban and travel ban may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain proper books, issuing false invoices, concealing beneficial ownership, or accepting untraced client funds through Stripe/Wise without customer due diligence as a regulated virtual CFO service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 500,000; license revocation by the Luxembourg regulatory authority; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years' imprisonment and a EUR 250,000 fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unauthorized disclosure and AML breaches; they face civil damages, restitution orders, and incarceration in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare Local/Master File when thresholds are met, or inability to prove arm's-length pricing for cross-border management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fixed monthly penalty up to EUR 1,000 per month per missing documentation; tax adjustment with markup or recharacterization of the transaction; late-interest surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for the corporate tax deficiency if they knowingly or negligently approved non-compliant intercompany policies, leading to personal asset seizure and travel restrictions.
